messages:
Samira K: Quick proposal — start a "soft exit" for v1 next week. Goal: route new traffic to v2 by default, but keep v1 as a quota-limited fallback for 30 days. Need input on routing policy, console copy, and how we show quota impact.
Matt R: Sounds reasonable. How aggressive is the default routing? 100% to v2 with a failover to v1, or split traffic during ramp?
Samira K: Default should be 95% -> v2, 5% -> v1 for first 3 days as probe, then 99/1. But enforce a per-tenant v1 quota (tokens/day) to cap cost and protect us.
Anika S: We should expose the quota preview in the console prior to flipping defaults. Tenants need to see estimated token delta if they stay on v1. Also: telemetry tag every request with `client_version` and `soft_exit_cohort` so we can slice regressions.
Jules P: Agree on telemetry. Also add a `fallback_reason` enum so we can tell if it fell back for capacity vs explicit pin.
Console UX: For the console, recommend a small badge on routes: "v2 preferred (v1 soft-exit)" with an inline "Preview impact" button that opens a modal showing projected tokens, cost delta, and a one-click opt-out slider. Keep copy non-alarmist.
Samira K: Example copy I'd like to test: "We recommend v2 for faster responses and lower costs. Your requests may be routed to v1 only as a limited fallback during the soft-exit. Click to preview how this affects your usage." Thoughts?
Matt R: Works. A couple of constraints: 1) If tenant pins v1 explicitly, they must bypass quota but trigger an exemption audit event. 2) If v2 capacity drops, we should automatically route back to v1 with a circuit-breaker and notify the tenant.
Anika S: About quotas: suggest a default soft quota = max(tenant_avg_tokens * 0.2, 10k tokens/day). Allow tenant-level override in the console. Also we need server-side enforcement + early-reject message `HTTP 429 {"error":"v1_quota_exceeded","hint":"Switch to v2 or request exemption"}`.
Console UX: UX for exemptions: add a small request form that creates a ticket for SEs, auto-populate tenant usage + suggested commit levels. Keep it gated to prevent abuse.
billing-bot: Note: any changes to quota behavior will affect billing projections. We need a nightly job to re-run forecasts for tenants in soft-exit and display "Estimated bill change" in modal.
Samira K: Good call, attach billing delta in modal. Also annotate the rollout in the rollout dashboard as "soft-exit:v1->v2" and emit events: `soft_exit.started`, `soft_exit.quota_violation`, `soft_exit.exemption_granted`.
Jules P: For telemetry schema, add these new events and a `soft_exit_version` field with values `v1`, `v2`, `v1_fallback`, `pinned_v1`. I'll draft the spec.
Matt R: Runbook items: 1) If `soft_exit.quota_violation` spike > 5% of tenants in 10m, pause rollout. 2) If error-rate for v2 increases by > 0.5% absolute vs baseline, auto-rollback to previous routing for 30m and page infra.
Console UX: Small copy tweak: change "opt-out slider" label to "Prefer legacy (v1) for this route" and show projected extra cost inline. Add a tooltip: "Choosing this reduces automatic safety fallback and increases your exposure to older model behavior."
Samira K: Ops question: how do we show historic comparisons? I want a chart with baseline (pre-soft-exit) vs current latency/cost per-1000 tokens by version.
Anika S: We'll emit a `metrics.tag` with `version` and `soft_exit_cohort`. The metrics pipeline can aggregate that. Chart query example: `sum(rate(tokens{version=\"v2\"}[1h])) by (tenant)` vs `sum(rate(tokens{version=\"v1\"}[1h]))`.
Samira K: Perf concern: telemetry tagging will increase cardinality. Can we limit cohort to `control|softexit` and avoid per-tenant tags in high-volume metrics?
Jules P: Yes: use low-cardinality tags for metrics, and send high-cardinality audit logs to our logging cluster for ad-hoc slices.
deploy-bot: deployment of routing-rule-service v3 succeeded in staging at 2023-10-11T14:02:33Z :white_check_mark:
Matt R: Final ask from infra: add a dry-run flag to the API so console can preview routing without committing. `POST /v1/routes/{id}/soft-exit-preview?dry_run=true` returns sample percentage splits + estimated cost.
Samira K: Perfect. Action items: Anika -> telemetry + quota enforcement spec; Jules -> event schema + runbook snippets; Console UX -> modal mocks + copy variants; Matt -> infra circuit-breaker thresholds + dry-run API; Samira -> rollout timeline and dashboard entry.
Console UX: I'll drop three copy variants into Figma by EOD and include token/cost mockups. :sparkles:
Samira K: Thanks all. We'll sync tomorrow 9:30 for sign-off. :thumbsup:
